races.name: Town And Country Cakes Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Just Johnny
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Alan Jones who has run his three career starts over 16-17f on Good ground, finishing no better than fifth; this 1m2f trip looks considerably shorter than ideal and Taylor Fisher faces a significant tactical challenge getting competitive from a cold position.

runners_data.name: Dialstone
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's lightly raced three-year-old with no public form to assess and going preference unknown; Edward Greatrex takes the ride for a yard operating at 7/48 over 14 days, so treat with caution until more is known.

runners_data.name: Liberate
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's lightly raced debutante last seen finishing fourth on Soft ground over 1m2f; the step up to firmer conditions is an open question, and Kaiya Fraser must deliver an improved showing on very limited evidence.

runners_data.name: Mother Dear
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partners this Hughie Morrison filly who has form that reads well here — a win over 1m2f on Good ground — and her prominent style makes her the most natural market rival to Egyptian Pharaoh for control of the race; the 38-day absence is worth noting but Hornby is a polished front-tracking partner.

runners_data.name: Adalo
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has run twice on Good ground without threatening, recording a sixth and a seventh; a natural hold-up horse whose best chance requires getting clean air from the rear, though the crowded hold-up sector in this race means Cieren Fallon may find it difficult to find its preferred position and rhythm.

runners_data.name: Egyptian Pharaoh
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the field who shapes to control proceedings from the outset for Oli Rix; OR 78 means rivals carry a class edge but Loughnane can dictate fractions on fast ground, and the tongue-tie is retained from previous starts where he has shown consistent placed form.

runners_data.name: Tinkety Tonk
runners_data.note: Kieran O'Neill partners this Hughie Morrison hold-up horse whose two career runs on Good ground have produced a fifth over 1m6f and a twelfth over 1m2f; nothing in the form encourages confidence, and sitting in a busy backmarker group only adds to the difficulty.

runners_data.name: Celestial Cen
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's lightly raced filly produced a promising runner-up effort on Soft ground over 1m2f, giving her the most concrete positive form among the unknowns; Pierre-Louis Jamin's booking adds interest and a step onto faster ground is the only real query for a yard operating at 2/32 over 14 days.

races.paceDynamic: Egyptian Pharaoh is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 1m2f Ffos Las contest and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, Billy Loughnane can dictate terms at whatever tempo suits on ground that has raced Good to Firm throughout the card. The hold-up horses — Just Johnny, Adalo, and Tinkety Tonk — must track from off the pace, while Mother Dear is the only prominent type capable of applying any pressure from close range. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically occupy the rear of the field, with Adalo redistributed to a midfield mapping position despite being a genuine hold-up horse, meaning its ability to switch off and get the true backmarker run it needs is compromised. With a single uncontested pace-setter able to control fractions on fast ground over a staying trip, this shape most strongly favours a prominent or tracking racer who travels smoothly in behind the leader and benefits from a strong gallop-on finish rather than a late sprint.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Egyptian Pharaoh Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Egyptian Pharaoh bowls along at a sustainable gallop and the hold-up pack cannot reel him in.
scenarios.body: If Egyptian Pharaoh bowls along at a sustainable gallop and the hold-up pack cannot reel him in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Pouncers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If Egyptian Pharaoh goes too quick early and the true hold-up horses get a target to run at from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: If Egyptian Pharaoh goes too quick early and the true hold-up horses get a target to run at from two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Mother Dear pressures Egyptian Pharaoh from the outset, turning the race into a tactical war of attrition.
scenarios.body: If Mother Dear pressures Egyptian Pharaoh from the outset, turning the race into a tactical war of attrition.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lightly Raced Type Improves
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed runners — Dialstone, Liberate, or Celestial Cen — steps forward significantly on debut or first try at the trip.
scenarios.body: If one of the unexposed runners — Dialstone, Liberate, or Celestial Cen — steps forward significantly on debut or first try at the trip.

watchPoints.text: Egyptian Pharaoh sets the entire pace map — if Loughnane slots into an uncontested lead before the first bend, the race is effectively run to his suit and all other runners are chasing his terms.

Mother Dear is the only horse likely to press Egyptian Pharaoh prominently; watch the opening two furlongs to see whether Rob Hornby elects to apply pressure or drops in, as that decision shapes the race tempo entirely.

Adalo's redistribution to midfield means Cieren Fallon may find the hold-up horses crowding each other out early; if Adalo cannot get a clean position and clear run, its chance diminishes sharply regardless of ability.

The Good to Firm surface is faster than the declared Going of Good — all six races at Ffos Las today are running Good to Firm — which will sharpen early fractions and may expose horses who have only run on soft or standard ground, notably Liberate and Celestial Cen.

Three lightly raced runners (Dialstone, Liberate, Celestial Cen) carry genuine form uncertainty; if any of them are notably well backed in the market, treat that as a significant information signal from connections.

races.name: West Wales Properties Pembrokeshire Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Dark Whisper
runners_data.note: Consistent placed form (2-3 over 8f on Good) makes this one of the more reliable profiles in the race; Billy Loughnane for David Menuisier is a strong booking, and the step up to 1m on good-to-firm suits given sim-going form is 2/2 placed.

runners_data.name: Impierious
runners_data.note: Twice placed over 8f on Good for Tom Clover, lightly raced but form reads consistently mid-pack; Kieran O'Neill is a capable pilot and the going is fine, though the horse has yet to demonstrate a decisive winning move in two runs.

runners_data.name: Ingemar
runners_data.note: Only run came over 10f on Good, so dropping back to 1m is an interesting trainer move from Brian Meehan; lightly raced with a single run showing fifth, the shorter trip could unlock more tactical speed, though the form is too thin to assess with confidence.

runners_data.name: Lean d'Aislingean
runners_data.note: Held-up style suits a race with a single front-runner if the pace is honest enough; both runs came on Soft which is notably different from today's good-to-firm, and the going switch is the primary concern for Edward Greatrex and Charlie Pike.

runners_data.name: Next Guilian
runners_data.note: Prominent style horse who carries a stamina question after fading late last time; Rod Millman's runner is expected to be active early and sit just off Kino Plasmat, but the fade flag is a meaningful warning against in a 1m race where the finish will be tested.

runners_data.name: Vincenzo Bellini
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Mark Loughnane whose trainer stats (0/20 T14) offer no encouragement; going is unknown and there is no form to assess, making this the most opaque runner in the field — a watching brief from Kaiya Fraser.

runners_data.name: Elenaya
runners_data.note: Returning from 192 days off for a two-year-old, which is significant; showed a placed run over 7f on Good but has the hold-up style that requires genuine pace, and the layoff combined with the longer trip makes this a speculative entry that George Bass will need to manage carefully with headgear noted.

runners_data.name: Kino Plasmat
runners_data.note: The race-shaping horse — sole front-runner for Ed Walker with Cieren Fallon in the saddle, who will have every opportunity to make all; ran fourth over 7f on Soft last time, so the step up to 1m on faster ground is a positive move, and the trainer's 5/28 T14 stat shows solid recent form.

races.paceDynamic: Kino Plasmat is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to apply pressure, Cieren Fallon can dictate terms from the front at whatever tempo suits, making this a classic lone-leader setup over a flat mile at Ffos Las. Dark Whisper and Next Guilian will push into prominent positions behind, but neither has the profile to seriously challenge for the lead, meaning Kino Plasmat faces zero early friction. The race will likely unfold as a steady-to-moderate gallop through the first half-mile before Fallon picks up the tempo entering the straight, leaving the field to respond on their own terms. This shape strongly favours either Kino Plasmat controlling and extending, or a well-positioned closer with a big engine who can pick off the leader in the final furlong — with the emphasis firmly on horses racing prominently or within two lengths of the pace, as a truly slow gallop will blunt any hold-up horse's finishing kick.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kino Plasmat Controls Freely
scenarios.trigger: If Kino Plasmat is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured, uncontested pace throughout.
scenarios.body: If Kino Plasmat is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a measured, uncontested pace throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Quicken Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady and Dark Whisper or Next Guilian track Kino Plasmat closely before pouncing in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely steady and Dark Whisper or Next Guilian track Kino Plasmat closely before pouncing in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and creates enough daylight for Lean d'Aislingean or Elenaya to run through beaten horses in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely honest and creates enough daylight for Lean d'Aislingean or Elenaya to run through beaten horses in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut/Lightly Raced Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Vincenzo Bellini or Ingemar, both unexposed, show unforeseen ability to overcome their limited form profiles.
scenarios.body: If Vincenzo Bellini or Ingemar, both unexposed, show unforeseen ability to overcome their limited form profiles.

watchPoints.text: Kino Plasmat — Cieren Fallon has a free lead and can set whatever tempo he chooses; if he controls the fractions through the first half-mile he may prove very difficult to reel in over the final two furlongs.

Next Guilian — flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, so watch the early gallop closely; if Darragh Keenan allows him to race too freely in the prominent position he favours, the fade could become a factor in running and compromise any horse caught in traffic behind him.

Lean d'Aislingean — both prior runs were on Soft, and today is Good to Firm; Edward Greatrex will need to monitor whether the horse handles the quicker surface in the early stages before committing to a hold-up ride.

Elenaya — 192 days off the track for a two-year-old is a notable flag; watch the paddock and early running to assess freshness, as a well-handicapped return could make this interesting despite the layoff.

Vincenzo Bellini — debut runner with no public form and a trainer operating at 0/20 over 14 days; the absence of any going or style intelligence makes this horse impossible to place tactically, and market moves before the off are the only available signal.

races.name: West Wales Properties Mayfair Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Angel's Call
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up type with a stamina flag — fades in the finish — and that is a serious concern over 7½f on quick ground; maps to midfield due to redistribution but true style is rear of field, and the 7-day turnaround with a poor sim-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 15 similar-ground runs) makes this hard to back.

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up filly dropping back slightly in trip after a placed effort at 8f on good ground; Harry Vigors takes the ride for Grace Harris whose recent 14-day strike rate is reasonable at 2/18, and three placed runs from eight on comparable going suggest she is competitive without being a winner.

runners_data.name: Belltony
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up runner whose true style is being compressed into a midfield berth — four-run form string of 7-4-6-5 shows consistency without conviction; no trainer runs in the 14-day window and only one of four comparable-going efforts ended in the frame, so the redistribution squeeze compounds an already modest profile.

runners_data.name: Blue Point Express
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse placed in the midfield slot, with headgear (p) in place and a patchy record on this type of going (0 wins, 0 places from 15 similar-ground runs); Adrian Wintle has been active with 3/19 in 14 days, but the form string of 8-9-5-0-5 offers little encouragement for a strong finish.

runners_data.name: King Of The Dance
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner in the race — seven-year-old with headgear (p), Cieren Fallon booked, and the cleanest profile to control this galloping 7½f track; 1 win and 3 places from 15 comparable-going runs shows he is not a pushover, and Bernard Llewellyn's 2/10 in 14 days adds stable confidence; STYLE_FIT tag is noted but he is naturally on the pace regardless.

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type who won on soft ground at 8f last time out and has placed at 8f on standard; Zoe Lewis claims 7lb which is significant, but the drop to 7½f and quick going are negatives — only 1 win from 15 similar-going efforts tells its own story, and he needs things to go wrong for the leader to capitalise.

runners_data.name: Spirited Dancer
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up filly who has been placed twice recently at 7f and 6f on good ground, giving her the most relevant recent form in the closer's camp; Billy Loughnane is a high-quality booking and the Kubler yard has been quiet at 0/5 in 14 days, but she is the most credible threat to King Of The Dance if she can track prominently.

runners_data.name: Mokata
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type carrying a "fades in finish" flag and an unbroken run of 0 wins, 0 places from all five comparable-going starts — all at this trip or beyond on good; Adam Kirby's 1/13 in 14 days is modest, headgear (tp) is in use, and the youngster looks out of depth at OR 46 in this shape.

runners_data.name: Snow Day
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly with the lowest OR in the field at 35 and a form string of 0-0-0-8 — the "fades in finish" flag is ominous; the redistribution into midfield from a true hold-up style only adds to her difficulties, and Tony Carroll's high-volume yard (6/37 in 14 days) rarely fires these types into big wins at this level.

races.paceDynamic: King Of The Dance is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — he should stride to the front from his draw and set a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground over 7½ furlongs at Ffos Las. With no pace rival to push him, the tempo is likely to be honest but not punishing, which historically at this course and distance allows a prominent horse to dictate and prove difficult to reel in late. The field is heavily weighted toward hold-up types — Angel's Call, Belltony, Blue Point Express, Mokata, and Snow Day are all true hold-up runners redistributed toward midfield on the map because there are more closers here than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear. This race shape strongly favours King Of The Dance's prominent-to-lead profile and any runner capable of tracking him in the slipstream through the first half, as the hold-up brigade will be fighting among themselves for a late run on a galloping track with limited give to accelerate off.

scenarios.title: King Of The Dance Dictates

scenarios.body: If King Of The Dance crosses cleanly and controls a measured tempo with no rival willing to race him for the lead.

scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften King Of The Dance and one hold-up runner threads through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften King Of The Dance and one hold-up runner threads through in the final furlong.

scenarios.title: Closers Dominate Late

watchPoints.text: King Of The Dance is the pivotal horse — if Cieren Fallon gets a clean break and establishes a lead unchallenged, the race shape is effectively set by the time the field enters the back straight.

Spirited Dancer bears watching in the early stages: if Billy Loughnane elects to track King Of The Dance rather than drop her in, she becomes a major player rather than a conventional closer in a race with very few genuine pace rivals.

The redistribution of Angel's Call, Belltony, Blue Point Express, Mokata, and Snow Day into midfield means the rear of the race will be congested — monitor the draw and early positioning as traffic complications in the straight are a real risk for this group.

Prince Ali's Zoe Lewis 7lb claim is worth watching in-running — if the pace is steady and Lewis manages to slot in behind the leader rather than settling deep, the claim could offset his otherwise modest profile on quick ground.

Going is reported as Good to Firm on the day (race-day report lists 7:09 7½f as Good to Firm), which is faster than the Good listed in the card header — any runner with a headgear flag or stamina concern should be re-evaluated for this surface upgrade before race-off.

races.name: WWP 34 Years Finding Customers Their Dream Homes Handicap

runners_data.name: Dappled Light
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent form including two wins, three placed efforts in 15 good-ground starts, and headgear applied — Adrian Wintle's six-year-old is well-suited to tracking a solo front-runner on this surface and should be ideally positioned throughout.|

runners_data.name: Sofian
runners_data.note: Nikki Evans' four-year-old returns after 105 days off but has a genuine win on good ground and a placed effort on Heathcock fast ground; a natural hold-up type who will need the pace to be strong enough to give Red Moon-style closers a chance to peg back a front-runner.|

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with modest recent form but has been placed twice in 15 good-ground runs; Rod Millman sends him here lightly weighted and Darragh Keenan takes the ride, though he needs a faster-than-expected gallop to get competitive at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Tonal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with headgear applied who has a legitimate win record at this kind of trip and goes well fresh (48 days); Billy Loughnane for Ian Williams (3 winners from 33 in 14 days) gives this some appeal as a pace-presser who could harry Quilt and ultimately benefit if the favourite fades.|

runners_data.name: Arnaz
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old has shown hold-up tendencies across all recent starts, but with several hold-up horses in this field his natural position at the rear cannot be guaranteed — Rob Hornby may find him racing in a more prominent midfield slot than suits, and the [STYLE_FIT] tag tempers his chance accordingly; trainer has had no winners from 17 runners in the past 14 days.|

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Zoe Lewis takes the 7lb claim for Bernard Llewellyn on this four-year-old who won over a mile and has placed at 7f, though her good-ground figures are thin (0 wins, 0 places from 3 runs); the claim could be meaningful if she can settle this prominent type close enough to land a blow.|

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's three-year-old is unexposed at 7½f (only four career runs), showed a placed effort at 7f on standard going, and has been off 57 days; Kaiya Fraser rides and the unknown style rating (U) leaves genuine uncertainty, but the unexposed profile at this trip is worth noting on good-to-firm ground.|

runners_data.name: Quilt
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old is the sole confirmed front-runner, and Cieren Fallon — a top-drawer pilot — should be able to control the race at whatever tempo suits from the front; Walker has five winners from 31 runners in the past 14 days, and Quilt's flat recent form (form: 455-39) is partly explained by unsuitable trips and conditions rather than loss of ability.|

runners_data.name: Red Moon
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's lightly-weighted three-year-old won over 7f on good ground 13 days ago and is clearly in form; a genuine hold-up type ridden by George Bass who is best served by a strong pace — if Quilt is pressured into going hard, Red Moon's profile becomes highly relevant in the closing stages.|

races.paceDynamic: Quilt is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge for the lead, Cieren Fallon should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the off on good-to-firm ground at Ffos Las. Dappled Light and Tonal are the two prominent types most likely to track Quilt closely, and with both carrying headgear their riders will want to be close to the action — that trio should establish the shape of the race from the first furlong. Red Moon and Sofian are the genuine hold-up horses at the back, but Arnaz — a natural hold-up type — has been redistributed to midfield because the field holds more off-the-pace horses than can all settle at the rear; Arnaz is unlikely to secure its true position and may end up racing out of role. A controlled pace set by a lone, uncontested front-runner on fast ground at a tight, galloping circuit favours horses who can track close to the pace and produce a measured, sustained finish — prominent and pace-pressing profiles are advantaged here over pure closers who need an end-to-end test.

watchPoints.text: Quilt's early tempo is the race-defining factor — if Cieren Fallon is allowed to bowl along unchallenged at a comfortable clip, the front-runner becomes very hard to catch on good-to-firm ground over 7½f at Ffos Las.

Tonal with headgear and Billy Loughnane is the most likely horse to press Quilt early — if these two engage in an early battle for supremacy, the pace will inflate and change the complexion of the race entirely.

Arnaz is mapped in midfield but is a natural hold-up type; watch whether Rob Hornby allows the horse to drop to the back or is forced wide and forward — racing out of role over 7½f is a meaningful negative for its chance.

Red Moon's winning run just 13 days ago (7f, good) is the freshest in-form angle in the field — if the pace is strong enough, George Bass may be able to produce a late run that catches the eye even if the front-runner has first run.

Medyg is the most unexposed runner in the race at this trip with only four career starts — any significant market move for Kaiya Fraser's mount should be noted as a possible yard confidence signal from Edward Smyth-Osbourne.

races.name: West Wales Properties Carmarthenshire Handicap

runners_data.name: Runamara
runners_data.note: Placed at 6f on Standard ground recently but limited to a best of 8th at 5f on Good, the step back to the minimum trip and a hold-up style in a race with no pace to track makes this a difficult profile; Taylor Fisher takes the ride for an in-form stable but the form figures at 5f on similar ground read 8/7/5 and there is little reason to expect improvement.|

runners_data.name: Forever Glamorous
runners_data.note: Christopher Mason's filly, who wore a hood previously, is placed at 5f on Soft and 6f on Good — the Good to Firm at Ffos Las is slightly quicker than her best form surface, but the 5f trip suits and Gina Mangan has a 2/7 trainer-jockey strike rate over 14 days; a natural hold-up type who will need to be positioned forward in practice given the shapeless pace.|

runners_data.name: Kodi K
runners_data.note: John Gallagher's three-year-old has a placed effort at 5f on Good ground and arrives just 12 days after his last run — Edward Greatrex rides, and while the horse is a genuine closer by inclination, the field's congestion at the rear means he will struggle to get the clean, covered passage a true hold-up type needs to deliver his best.|

runners_data.name: Magnificent Mel
runners_data.note: Dual-placed at 5f and 6f on Good ground for Rod Millman, Magnificent Mel has a solid placing profile but six starts produce no wins — Darragh Keenan rides and the trainer has sent out 2 from 25 over 14 days; though naturally suited to coming late, the reality of this race shape means he will likely end up racing closer than ideal without truly leading.|

runners_data.name: My Mate Mackley
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby trains this horse, who won at 5f on Soft and placed third at 5f on Soft — the step up to Good to Firm is a surface query worth flagging, but Billy Loughnane is a top booking and the horse has both the right trip and the profile of a runner who may well find himself pressing forward in a leaderless field; the headgear (p) is a positive trigger.|

runners_data.name: Follow My Heart
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's second string, ridden by Cieren Fallon who has a 1/19 14-day strike rate for the yard — Follow My Heart's form figures of 9/5/4/6/9 across varying tracks read as a horse that rarely threatens to win, and while it placed fourth on Good ground at 6f, the 5f on Good to Firm at Ffos Las is a new combination; the natural hold-up style is the least helpful profile in this shapeless race.|

runners_data.name: Tanaka
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's runner arrives just 7 days after his last race having won at 5f on Good ground — Rob Hornby, who rides for a powerful stable posting 6/58 over 14 days, partners a horse whose headgear tag (h) suggests he races with cover in mind; however, in a field where no one wants to lead, Tanaka's recent 5f win on identical ground makes him the horse most likely to find himself dictating by default, which is a significant tactical asset.|

races.paceDynamic: This 5f sprint at Ffos Las on Good to Firm ground is a peculiar shape: not a single confirmed front-runner in the field, leaving the race wide open for whoever is most willing to bowl along from the gates. With every runner officially coded as a hold-up type, the early fractions will be set by whichever horse breaks sharpest and finds themselves in front by default rather than design — a scrambled, pace-by-accident scenario that typically produces a messy, bunched finish. Tanaka, who won over 5f on Good ground last time, and My Mate Mackley, who has won over 5f on Soft, are the two most likely to find themselves prominently positioned through circumstance if their rivals drift and settle. The race shape strongly favours any runner comfortable racing handily or close to a muddling pace, as true hold-up horses will find little cover to latch on to and no sustained gallop to aim at — compact, sprint finishers who handle a falsely-run 5f are the primary beneficiaries. Note that Magnificent Mel, Kodi K, My Mate Mackley, Follow My Heart, and Tanaka are all genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because the field has more such horses than the shape can accommodate at the rear, and none of them is likely to get a clean, patient ride from the back in practice.

scenarios.title: Outsider Capitalises On Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the confused pace shape creates a gap on the rail or a split that allows a lesser-fancied runner to steal through uncontested.
scenarios.body: If the confused pace shape creates a gap on the rail or a split that allows a lesser-fancied runner to steal through uncontested.

watchPoints.text: Watch Tanaka's early stride — if Rob Hornby finds himself in front inside the first furlong with no natural pace-setter to challenge, he effectively becomes the race's de facto leader and the whole dynamic shifts in his favour.

My Mate Mackley's surface suitability is the key variable: all winning and placed form is on Soft or Standard ground, and a move to Good to Firm at Ffos Las tonight is an untested jump that could blunt the finishing effort Billy Loughnane will be looking for.

Forever Glamorous wore headgear previously — check if she lines up in the hood tonight, as the hood runners at Ffos Las in this grade have a notable recent record and it materially changes how she is likely to be ridden by Gina Mangan.

With every runner a hold-up type, watch the draw and early positioning in the stalls — whoever breaks quickest from the gates gets the rail or the lead by default, and in a 5f sprint on Good to Firm that positional accident could be decisive regardless of intended race style.

Monitor the in-running market drift at the off — if two or more runners are backed as if they expect to be covered up, any late money for Tanaka or My Mate Mackley pressing forward would be a strong signal that connections have read the muddling pace shape correctly.

races.name: West Wales Properties Ceredigion Handicap

runners_data.name: Bulldog Spirit
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Bernard Llewellyn who has shown fair form at 2m on good ground (6th from 15 starters in similar conditions); Cieren Fallon is a useful booking, last ran 30 days ago and arrives fresh, but needs the pace to be genuine to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Merrijig
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won over 16f on standard and placed three times in that distance band; Gina Mangan rides, 22 days since last run, the blinker/cheekpieces entry is worth noting, and her best form at similar trips on good ground makes her one of the more interesting closers if gaps appear.

runners_data.name: Oakley
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter whose record on good to firm is outstanding (3 wins, 9 places from 12 runs); long lay-off of 275 days is the chief concern and the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reminds that racing prominently is not his entirely natural mode, yet his role here as lone front-runner is structurally dominant regardless.

runners_data.name: Golden Flame
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type resuming after a lengthy 264-day absence; Charlie & Mark Johnston have had no runners in the past 14 days, her best form came on softer ground, and the quick conditions and extreme layoff make this a watch-and-see run for Zoe Lewis (7) on debut for connections.

runners_data.name: Simiyann
runners_data.note: Ian Williams runner who wears a visor and is a genuine hold-up horse remapped to midfield because the rear is over-subscribed; Billy Loughnane is an in-form booking (1 win from 27 in the T14 window) and if he pushes forward early could turn this into a two-horse contest with Oakley, though his best figures came on softer ground.

runners_data.name: Chillhi
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse who carries tongue-tie and blinkers and has been given a 64-day freshener (7 jockeys); Tyrese Cameron (5) rides, trainer Barry John Murphy is in good form (T14: 3/7), and Chillhi's previous 3rd in a 22f chase-distance race shows stamina, but being a redistributed type limits his chance if he cannot secure a forward pitch.

runners_data.name: Cogital
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old for Bernard Llewellyn — the trainer also saddles Bulldog Spirit and Adrian — returning after 61 days and 27 jockeys, suggesting a less straightforward campaign; Harry Vigors (5) rides and the horse did win at 17f on good, though his recent form (3-8-3-9-5) is patchy and he is a natural hold-up type squeezed further forward by the field's composition.

runners_data.name: Sapphire Sirocco
runners_data.note: Five-year-old in form — won last time out 17 days ago over 17f on good ground — for Barry John Murphy, who also trains Chillhi; Ryan Kavanagh (5) gets the ride and the recent win at exactly this type of trip and surface gives him a live profile, even if his true hold-up style means he relies on getting a clean run from what will likely be a bunched mid-pack.

runners_data.name: Adrian
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's third runner in the race, wearing blinkers, last seen 26 days ago; his best handicap form has come on softer going and all five recent runs show he struggles to get competitive on faster surfaces, while being a hold-up type in an overcrowded rear does not help his tactical position with Kieran O'Neill.

runners_data.name: Oceanides
runners_data.note: Four-year-old for Ed de Giles with a clear tendency to fade in the closing stages — flagged as such — and all recent form on softer surfaces than today's good to firm; Olivia Tubb (5) takes the mount 26 days after the last run, but the combination of inexperience, ground concern and finishing fade make this one to treat cautiously at 2m.

runners_data.name: Marinakis
runners_data.note: Declared non-runner; no further analysis applicable, though his removal tightens the field to 10 effective runners and marginally reduces the hold-up horse congestion at the rear.

races.paceDynamic: Oakley is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 2m handicap at Ffos Las, and with no genuine rival to press him from the outset, he is set to control the tempo from flag to finish on good to firm ground — a surface where he holds a strong record (3W9P in similar conditions). The pace is unlikely to be truly fierce; Oakley can dictate at a comfortable gallop around this flat circuit, which historically punishes horses who try to come from deep and rewards those racing within sight of the leader. Although several runners in this field — Simiyann, Chillhi, Cogital, Sapphire Sirocco, Adrian, Oceanides and Marinakis — are true hold-up types redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded, the field does contain more hold-up and prominent preferences than can all fulfil their natural position, and Simiyann and Chillhi are the most likely to press forward and attempt to claim prominent berths. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently or just off the steady pace Oakley sets, allowing them to be delivered with a controlled challenge in the straight rather than having to make up ground from a bunched, slowly-strung-out rear group.

watchPoints.text: Oakley's 275-day absence is the single biggest race-shape risk — if he returns ring-rusty and surrenders his lead early, the entire pace structure collapses and the race becomes unpredictable; watch him in the parade ring and in the early strides for any sign of reluctance to stride on.

Simiyann (Billy Loughnane) and Chillhi (Tyrese Cameron) may both attempt to push forward from their natural hold-up positions; if both press Oakley before halfway, the pace lifts sharply and stamina becomes the decisive factor rather than tactical speed.

Sapphire Sirocco won over 17f on good ground just 17 days ago and arrives in peak condition — if he gets a clean passage from a midfield position on the flat Ffos Las straight, his in-form status makes him a live danger regardless of the tactical shape.

Barry John Murphy saddles two runners (Chillhi and Sapphire Sirocco) and Bernard Llewellyn saddles three (Bulldog Spirit, Cogital, Adrian) — stable tactics between these pairs could influence early positioning and should be watched from the stalls.

The going report consistently logs good to firm for this final race of the card across all six races, confirming the surface has not changed — horses with a concern flag on quick ground are unlikely to be flattered by conditions that have only got faster through the evening.
